mutations.label: Nothing wrong
mutations.what: A well-formed token from the issuer, made for this surface.
mutations.teaches: The baseline: every check passes.

mutations.label: Wrong issuer
mutations.what: iss names a different issuer that nobody configured.
mutations.teaches: Trust starts with the issuer string. An issuer you did not register is refused before anything else is looked at.

mutations.label: Trailing slash on the issuer
mutations.what: iss is the configured string with a slash added, or taken off if it had one.
mutations.teaches: Issuer matching is exact. Auth0 and Microsoft v1.0 end in a slash, so this is the commonest mistake.

mutations.label: Different case in the issuer
mutations.what: The first letter of the host in iss is upper-case.
mutations.teaches: Host names are not case-sensitive on the network, but the issuer comparison is.

mutations.label: Wrong audience
mutations.what: aud is a different API.
mutations.teaches: The audience binds a token to one recipient. Without it a token for one API works on another.

mutations.label: Expired
mutations.what: exp was an hour ago.
mutations.teaches: Every surface checks exp. A little clock skew is tolerated, an hour is not.

mutations.label: Not yet valid
mutations.what: nbf is an hour in the future.
mutations.teaches: nbf is checked wherever it is present. Some issuers never set it.

mutations.label: Lifetime too long
mutations.what: exp is 30 days after iat.
mutations.teaches: Only some surfaces cap how long a token may live, and they cap it in different ways.

mutations.label: No exp
mutations.what: The exp claim is left out.
mutations.teaches: A token with no expiry never stops being valid, so surfaces insist on one.

mutations.label: No iat
mutations.what: The iat claim is left out.
mutations.teaches: Some issuers do not issue iat. A surface that requires it will refuse them.

mutations.label: Different subject
mutations.what: sub is another workload or user.
mutations.teaches: Only a surface that pins the subject notices. Elsewhere any subject from a trusted issuer gets in.

mutations.label: A pinned claim is missing
mutations.what: The one extra claim the surface is told to require is left out.
mutations.teaches: Requiring a claim is how you tell one workload or repository from another, and only some surfaces can do it.

mutations.label: Tampered signature
mutations.what: One character of the signature is changed.
mutations.teaches: Any change to a signed token breaks the signature.

mutations.label: No signature (alg none)
mutations.what: The header says alg none and the signature is empty.
mutations.teaches: An unsigned token proves nothing. Every surface refuses it.

mutations.label: HMAC instead of RSA (HS256)
mutations.what: The token is signed with HMAC, using the issuer's public key as the secret.
mutations.teaches: The classic key-confusion attack. A surface must pin the algorithm family, not trust the header.

mutations.label: Encrypted (nested) token
mutations.what: The token has five parts, as an encrypted JWT does.
mutations.teaches: A surface cannot read the claims of an encrypted token, so none of them accepts one.

mutations.label: Signed with a key nobody published
mutations.what: The signature is valid but the key id is not in the issuer's key set.
mutations.teaches: A rotated or rogue key is refused. After a rotation the key set must be refreshed.

mutations.label: Token type named as access_token
mutations.what: The exchange calls the third-party token an access_token.
mutations.teaches: PingOne wants urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt for a third-party token.

mutations.label: Issuer not assigned to the application
mutations.what: The issuer exists but the calling application was never given it.
mutations.teaches: A trusted issuer does nothing until it is assigned to an application.

mutations.label: Identity switched off
mutations.what: The Federated Identity has Enabled set to false.
mutations.teaches: Enabled is the only kill switch. A valid token from a disabled identity is refused.

mutations.label: Wrong header typ
mutations.what: The header typ is JWT, not oauth-id-jag+jwt.
mutations.teaches: An ID-JAG is a specific kind of token. A plain JWT from a trusted IdP is not one.

mutations.label: Resource not listed
mutations.what: The resource in the assertion is not on the token manager.
mutations.teaches: PingFederate issues only for the resources a token manager lists. Anything else is invalid_target.

pf-idjag.note: The checks our resource server lists include exp and iat but no not-before check.

p1-exchange.note: Only because Max Future Validity is set. At 0 any future date is valid.

p1az-oauth.note: The documented checks have no lifetime cap: exp only has to be in the future.

pf-idjag.note: The checks our resource server lists have no lifetime cap.

p1-exchange.note: Only because Require Issued-at Claim is on.
The documented settings have nothing that pins a subject.

p1az-oauth.note: The external OAuth server does basic access control only. Decisions on claims need custom policies.

pf-idjag.note: sub is the person. The redeemer does not pin it.

p1-exchange.note: The documented settings have no required-claims list.

pf-idjag.note: Here the missing claim is client_id, which the ID-JAG draft requires.

p1-exchange.note: The key set holds RSA keys, which cannot verify an HMAC. PingOne's own text for this case was not measured.
PingOne's own text for an unknown key id was not measured.

p1az-oauth.note: An unknown kid triggers a fresh JWKS fetch; if the key is still not there the signature is invalid.
